threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground' and look puzzled at the bus stops. Classic newbie move.
Last night on the 59, a couple tried to argue their way out of a £50 fine for not tapping in. They insisted the driver had winked at them first.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a group of kids roller-skating past a kebab stand blaring Beethoven, I knew this place had a pulse of its own.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain do you find spontaneous punk shows in abandoned buildings, blending gritty charm with a wild energy you won't find anywhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can spot a tourist just looking at the BART map, but barely grimace at another Muni delay from a dog on the tracks.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a rider serenading passengers with a ukulele at Civic Center despite the delays. Only in SF do breakdowns spark live music.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'Gràcia' is just for the parks and plazas; they miss the old factories turned into art studios, full of local character.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their confusion at the lack of straws in cafes—still ordering drinks the 'old' way, missing the local tapas hustle.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' when it’s clearly the Overground here. Local lingo is crucial, mate. Better learn fast!
Caught a guy on the 133 last night arguing with a lamp post like it had wronged him. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When a random street musician on Flughafenstrasse played a chilling rendition of 'Adele' as the tram rolled by, and everyone stopped to listen.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you catch a bus with a DJ spinning behind the driver. It's like public transport meets a block party, every weekend!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know they're locals when they casually complain about the half-cooked burritos from that new taco spot and continue to buy from La Taqueria.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a tuxedo calmly waiting for the bus while juggling three pineapples. Only in the Tenderloin does that feel totally normal.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the parks, but they miss the nuanced charm of our hidden plazas filled with locals just sharing a vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by how they flock to the tourist traps on Carrer Verdi, still oblivious to the gems just a few streets away.
